note: A margin on a bare element is prose, not layout drift: layout/margin-on-child passes a stylesheet rule whose every selector keys on a tag with no class of its own (lines 1, 5, 7 for li:not(.x), and the nested p on 12), tokenized or not. h2 (line 4) names no class, so the rule is never read. A class-keyed rule keeps the verdict, a tokenized margin included (2, 6, 8, 13); so do the universal * of an owl selector (9) and a list with one classed selector (10). A bleed on a p is still layout/negative-margin (3). An inline style and a CSS-in-JS template, its nested p group included, have no stylesheet rule to read and keep firing (Card.jsx 4, 9, 15).
